\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دبیرستان} (dabirestân)}{دبیرستان (dabirestân)}]{\fa{دبیرستان} (dabirestân) — a secondary school}

\label{lesson:FA-C155-dabirestan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a café, then the Persian for a doctor's surgery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دبیرستان}}
\textbf{\fa{دبیرستان}} — \emph{dabirestân} — \textquotedblleft{}a secondary school\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dabirestân} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed: it continues Middle Persian \emph{dibīrestān}, \textquotedblleft{}school\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). It is \emph{dabir}, \textquotedblleft{}scribe, teacher\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-estân}, \textquotedblleft{}place of\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کلانتری} (kalântari)}{کلانتری (kalântari)}]{\fa{کلانتری} (kalântari) — a police station}

\label{lesson:FA-C155-kalantari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a doctor's surgery, then the Persian for a secondary school.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کلانتری}}
\textbf{\fa{کلانتری}} — \emph{kalântari} — \textquotedblleft{}a police station\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kalântari} is built from \emph{kalântar}, \textquotedblleft{}headman\textquotedblright{}, and the ending \emph{-i}, \textquotedblleft{}office of\textquotedblright{}. \emph{kalântar} is \emph{kalân}, \textquotedblleft{}big\textquotedblright{}, with the comparative \emph{-tar}: \textquotedblleft{}the bigger one\textquotedblright{}. All the pieces are native Persian, inherited rather than borrowed.
\end{cousinweb}

Before the new one: say the Persian for a secondary school, then the Persian for a police station.

\textbf{\fa{شهرداری}} — \emph{shahrdâri} — \textquotedblleft{}the town hall\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shahrdâri} is \emph{shahr}, \textquotedblleft{}city\textquotedblright{} (Middle Persian \emph{šahr}, EtymDB), with \emph{dâr}, \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{} (from \emph{dâshtan}), and \emph{-i}: the office that holds the city. All are native.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گمرک} (gomrok)}{گمرک (gomrok)}]{\fa{گمرک} (gomrok) — customs}

\label{lesson:FA-C155-gomrok}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the town hall, then the Persian for an embassy.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گمرک}}
\textbf{\fa{گمرک}} — \emph{gomrok} — \textquotedblleft{}customs\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gomrok} goes back to Byzantine Greek \emph{kommerkion}, \textquotedblleft{}customs duty\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{commercium}, \textquotedblleft{}trade\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); it is usually said to have reached Persian through Turkish \emph{gümrük}.
\end{cousinweb}
